title: Marcos gave ‘diplomatic’ response to Trump’s single-supplier proposal
summary: President Marcos only gave a “diplomatic” response to US President Donald Trump’s suggestion that the Philippines source all its energy and agricultural imports from the United…

blocks.text: US President Donald Trump (L) and Philippines' President Ferdinand Marcos Jr attend a luncheon at Malacanang Palace in Manila on Nov. 18, 2026.

MANILA, Philippines — President Marcos only gave a “diplomatic” response to US President Donald Trump’s suggestion that the Philippines source all its energy and agricultural imports from the United States, Philippine Ambassador to the US Jose Manuel Romualdez said.
In an interview with “Storycon” on One News yesterday, Romualdez denied that Marcos responded with “yes, sir” when Trump proposed a single-supplier trade arrangement for the Philippines.
“President Marcos said, ‘if it can be supplied from the United States, why not?’ That’s essentially the essence of the conversation,” Romualdez said.
The ambassador stressed that any commitment would depend on negotiations between the two longtime allies, including discussions on costs and the feasibility of the proposal.

“The commitments, of course, will have to come after we have a complete discussion on how we’re going to be able to achieve the proposal of President Trump,” he said. “But at the end of the day, it’s a trade deal, which means you say both parties have to look at the cost and how it would be able to get to that point.”
While recognizing the close relationship between the Philippines and the US, Romualdez said economic considerations would remain crucial in determining whether the proposal could be pursued.
“If it can be supported by the United States at a cheaper price, (then why not?),” Romualdez said.
“We’re open to the possibility. That’s (the message that) President Marcos sent… When you have a meeting like this, you don’t close the door and say, ‘no, we can’t do that,’” he added.
